title: The Stage Without a Center
fact_notes: 人物・制度・具体的な出来事は架空の教材例・思考実験。実在の調査・統計・実証結果を示すものではない。制作台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: A fictional dance group was invited to perform in a community hall where the audience would sit on three sides of the stage.
sentences.ja: 架空のダンスグループは観客が舞台の三方向に座る地域ホールで踊るよう招かれた。

sentences.en: The dancers had originally developed their performance for a theater with a clearly defined front and back.
sentences.ja: ダンサーは当初、明確な前後のある劇場向けに演目を作っていた。

sentences.en: Many movements were designed to direct attention toward a single performer standing at the center of the stage.
sentences.ja: 動きの多くは舞台中央の一人に注意を向けるよう設計されていた。

sentences.en: When the group rehearsed in the new hall, however, they discovered that important gestures were hidden from some parts of the audience.
sentences.ja: しかし新ホールで練習すると一部の観客席から重要な身振りが見えないことが分かった。

sentences.en: At first, the director suggested simply repeating every important movement while facing each section of the audience in turn.
sentences.ja: 当初、演出家は観客席の各区画を順に向いて重要な動きを繰り返すことを提案した。

sentences.en: Although this would make the gestures visible to more people, it would also interrupt the rhythm of the original performance.
sentences.ja: 身振りをより多くの人に見せられるが元の演目のリズムも途切れるだろう。

sentences.en: Another dancer proposed considering the different viewpoints as an artistic possibility rather than merely a practical obstacle.
sentences.ja: 別のダンサーは異なる視点を実用上の障害でなく芸術上の可能性と考える案を出した。

sentences.en: Instead of making every spectator see exactly the same action, the group could design movements that offered different but connected experiences.
sentences.ja: すべての観客に全く同じ動作を見せず、異なるが関連した経験を提供する動きを設計できる。

sentences.en: The dancers experimented with arrangements in which small groups performed related movements at different places on the stage.
sentences.ja: 小グループが舞台の異なる場所で関連する動きをする配置を試した。

sentences.en: A gesture initiated by one dancer might be continued by another at the opposite end of the performance area.
sentences.ja: 一人が始めた身振りを反対側にいる別のダンサーが継続することもあった。

sentences.en: They recorded the rehearsal from three positions and examined whether each perspective provided enough information to follow the development of the dance.
sentences.ja: 三地点から練習を録画し各視点で踊りの展開を追う十分な情報が得られるか調べた。

sentences.en: The group adjusted several transitions after noticing that a sequence meaningful from one position appeared disconnected from another.
sentences.ja: 一つの位置では意味のある連続動作が別の位置からはばらばらに見えたため、いくつかの移行を調整した。

sentences.en: Before the public performance, the dancers invited a small audience to describe what they had noticed without providing a detailed explanation in advance.
sentences.ja: 公開公演前に少人数の観客を招き事前の詳細説明なしに気づいたことを述べてもらった。

sentences.en: Their accounts varied, but several people described relationships between movements that the director had not deliberately planned.
sentences.ja: 感想は異なったが演出家が意図していなかった動きの関係を述べる人もいた。

sentences.en: The dancers welcomed these interpretations while recognizing that an unexpected response was not automatically evidence of successful communication.
sentences.ja: 予想外の反応が自動的に伝達成功の証拠ではないと認識しながら解釈を歓迎した。

sentences.en: They revised parts that appeared consistently confusing and retained differences that contributed to the richness of the experience.
sentences.ja: 一貫して分かりにくい部分を修正し経験の豊かさに貢献する違いは残した。

sentences.en: The example illustrates that an artistic work can respond to the conditions under which people encounter it.
sentences.ja: この例は芸術作品が人々の出会う条件に応じ得ることを示す。

sentences.en: A change in physical space may challenge established conventions while creating possibilities that were unavailable in the original setting.
sentences.ja: 物理空間の変化は既存の慣習に挑み元の環境にはなかった可能性を生み得る。

sentences.en: The group learned that artistic coherence does not necessarily require every spectator to receive identical information at exactly the same moment.
sentences.ja: 芸術的な一貫性には必ずしも全観客が同じ瞬間に同一情報を得る必要はないと学んだ。

sentences.en: It requires careful attention to the relationships that make each particular experience meaningful.
sentences.ja: それぞれの経験を意味あるものにする関係への注意深い配慮が必要だ。

vocabulary.definition: quality of being full or varied

questions.prompt: How was the new hall different?
options: The audience sat on three sides.

questions.prompt: Why did the original choreography cause difficulty?
options: The stage had no lighting at all.
Some gestures were invisible from certain seats.
questions.explanation_ja: 一部の席から見えない。

questions.prompt: What drawback did repeating gestures have?
options: It could interrupt the original rhythm.
questions.explanation_ja: リズムを損なう可能性。

questions.prompt: What new artistic idea was proposed?
options: Use different viewpoints to offer connected but varied experiences.
questions.explanation_ja: 異なる視点を創造的に活用。

questions.prompt: How did they examine the revised dance?
options: Asked only the director to watch.
They wanted no connection between movements.
Some sequences looked disconnected from certain positions.
questions.explanation_ja: 視点によって連続性が失われた。

questions.prompt: Why not equate every unexpected response with success?
options: Unexpected interpretations might also indicate confusion.
Only the director can interpret art.
The audience was not allowed to speak.

questions.explanation_ja: 豊かさをもたらす違い。

options: Spatial constraints can become artistic opportunities if viewpoints are considered carefully.
Every performance must be identical from all seats.
Artistic value is unrelated to audience experience.
Repeating all gestures solves every problem.
questions.explanation_ja: 空間の制約を芸術的可能性に変える。

grammar.focus: Although this would make the gestures visible
whether each perspective provided enough information

grammar.explanation_ja: 必ずしも〜を必要としない。

paraphrases.source: When the group rehearsed in the new hall, however, they discovered that important gestures were hidden from some parts of the audience.
paraphrases.rewrite: At rehearsal they saw that some seats offered no view of important gestures.

paraphrases.source: Although this would make the gestures visible to more people, it would also interrupt the rhythm of the original performance.
paraphrases.rewrite: Repeating the movements could improve visibility but disrupt the rhythm.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 視認性とリズムの両立課題。

paraphrases.source: They recorded the rehearsal from three positions and examined whether each perspective provided enough information to follow the development of the dance.
paraphrases.rewrite: They compared views to see if spectators could follow the dance from each position.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 各視点で展開を追えるか。

paraphrases.source: The group learned that artistic coherence does not necessarily require every spectator to receive identical information at exactly the same moment.
paraphrases.rewrite: A coherent performance need not give every viewer exactly the same information at the same time.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 同一情報は必須でない。

discourse.role_ja: 元の設計と新会場の問題。

cloze.explanation_ja: 異なる視点を障害だけと見ない。
一貫して混乱する部分。
